properties.label: Sisimiut → Kangerluarsuk Tulleq
properties.description: This day is one of the toughest but also has some of the most beautiful vistas. It starts by following the southern edge of the fjord across numerous rivers and through boggy areas before ascending steeply up the appropriately named "Murder Hill". The trail then undulates along a high valley and offers a spectacular view over the Nasaasaaq Mountain range before descending steeply into Sisimiut. There is also the option of following the Oqummiannguaq trail into town to avoid the last section of ATV track.

properties.label: Kangerluarsuk Tulleq → Nerumaq
properties.description: This section of the trail runs along the base of the Nerumaq Valley, featuring swampy terrain, dense willow bushes, and several river crossings. The difficulty of the crossings may vary based on weather conditions. Hikers have two accommodation options: a larger hut by the fjord (with no clearly marked trail leading to it) or a smaller hut located on a hill, accessible via the main trail.

properties.label: Nerumaq → Innajuatooq
properties.description: This trail segment starts by crossing the wide river and following the northern edge of the lake. It then climbs to a low ridge above the valley floor, tracing the base of the mountains before making a sharp turn to arrive at the hut. Certain sections of the trail may be difficult to discern, as they can be overgrown with willow bushes or obscured by boggy terrain. However, staying within the valley and keeping an eye out for cairns will help guide your way.

properties.label: Innajuatooq → Eqalugaarniarfik
properties.description: The trail ascends out of the UNESCO-protected area to a ridgeline, where hikers are rewarded with panoramic views of numerous lakes and distant mountain ranges. From there, it descends into boggier terrain as it winds its way past several lakes before entering a wide valley. Following the course of a broad river, hikers encounter two huts. The first is perched on the hillside and small. The second, much larger, sits by the lake and is every hiker's favorite.

properties.label: Eqalugaarniarfik → Ikkattooq
properties.description: The trail ascends steeply to a plateau with large erratic boulders that were left behind by the receding glacier. Just before a very steep descent, hikers are rewarded with one of the trail’s most iconic vistas—the lookout over the Itinneq River valley. This is the trail's deepest river crossing. It is usually fordable in summer, or there is a bridge nearby (from 2025). Afterward, the trail crosses boggy terrain before ascending toward the Eqalugaarniarfik Hut.

properties.label: Ikkattooq → Canoe Centre
properties.description: This trail sector offers incredible views as it transitions from scenic lakes, past the famous beach, to a high, rocky plateau that is part of the Aasivissuit-Nipisat UNESCO area. There are boggy stretches where the trail becomes indistinct (follow the cairns), and a steep climb that where you are rewarded with panoramic views over the landscape.

properties.label: Canoe Centre → Katiffik
properties.description: This section of the trail along the southern shore of Lake Amitsorsuaq offers mostly flat walking. However, it includes a challenging stretch where large boulders create difficulty, particularly when the lake's water level is high. If you are lucky, you can canoe this section of trail. Note: canoes should never be paddled west of the Canoe Centre.

properties.label: Katiffik → Kellyville
properties.description: The trail features a variety of landscapes, including brackish lakes near Kangerlussuaq, freshwater lakes, and rolling hills. While the trail tread is generally easy to follow, it becomes less distinct in boggy areas, which are common. Hikers will encounter two steep ascents and one steep descent leading down to the Katiffik Hut.
